_readme: Farm scene spec — the art seam for the living farm (web/src/farm.ts).
This file is the SINGLE source of truth for where creatures may stand and how
big they are against the scene; the engine reads it at load (loadFarmSpec) and
needs no code change when the art does.
width/height    scene units (any unit — the view scales the whole layer to fit)
walkable        rectangle the creatures' FEET stay inside {x,y,w,h}
spriteSize      creature box, in the same scene units, at the front of the zone
depthScaleFar   sprite scale at the BACK edge of walkable (the depth cue)
depthScaleNear  sprite scale at the FRONT edge of walkable
minSpacing      closest two creatures may stand, centre to centre
props           static scenery inside the walkable band, y-sorted with the cast
Every field is required: a partial file is rejected in favour of the engine
default (farm.ts parseFarmSpec) rather than mixing art and defaults.
── PAINTED SCENE LANDED · Flamingo (Designer) · 2026-07-17 ──
Placeholders replaced with the real numbers. Art direction, layer/z-order
table and the rules behind these values: docs/FARM-SCENE-SPEC.md
width/height = the layer SVGs' shared viewBox — farm-sky / farm-hills /
farm-ground / farm-backdrop / farm-foreground / farm-fx are all 1600x900 and
self-align when stacked at inset:0 with object-fit:cover.
WALKABLE — a RECT, and that is a DECISION, not a stopgap (CEO, 2026-07-17):
FarmSpec takes an axis-aligned RECT. The painted ground is a TRAPEZOID —
perspective, so the mown pen is wider at the front than at the back:
back edge  y=520, x  300 -> 1300
front edge y=830, x   90 -> 1510
The rect below is the largest one fitting ENTIRELY inside that trapezoid: it
takes the narrow BACK edge's width and holds it forward, so every point the
sim can pick lands on painted mown grass — safe by construction, and the
system carries ONE geometry instead of a rect in the engine and a trapezoid
in our heads drifting apart again.
The cost is the two front corners. We buy those back in ART, never in code:
fence and bushes close the corners off so the rect reads as a pen we meant to
build, not a pen that got cut. Do NOT add a depth-aware clamp to reclaim them.
SPRITE SIZE — species SVGs are viewBox 0 0 200 200, drawn into a square box:
216 units at the front edge, 104 at the back (216 * 0.4833). That 2.07x range
is what makes walking toward the camera read as depth rather than as a sticker
scaling up. Creatures are intentionally oversized vs the barn — this is a
creature collector, the cast reads first. Not a bug, please don't 'fix' it.
MIN SPACING — measured off the art, not chosen by feel:
The 216 box is mostly padding; the painted body fills only 55-70% of it
(web/scripts/measure-sprite-body.mjs reads every species' real bbox through
Chrome's getBBox). Widest body = sproutling at 70% = 151.2 units at the front
edge. 152 is that worst case rounded up, so the two widest creatures standing
shoulder to shoulder at the closest, largest point of the pen just touch and
never overlap. Anywhere further back they cannot reach each other at all.
farm.ts applies minSpacing flat at every depth, so it MUST be sized on the
front edge — the only place bodies are full size. If the sprite box or the
species art changes, re-run the measure script; do not re-guess.
COUPLED TO THE ART: the lantern-post prop at (792, 790) and the fence lanterns
have their light pools PAINTED INTO farm-ground.svg at (330,640), (1268,620),
(792,784). Move a lantern and the glow stays behind — ping Flamingo.
